verdictStatement: The subject's carry discipline is excellent and I could not break it: the DR-124 row is byte-exact against the live register, the file 04 state-class block is 13/13 byte-exact, both architecture-source digests match live, and every scoping disclaimer the dispatch told me to attack (SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, implementation authorization, CD-RT-5 applied to SC-OPS, an invented purge/D9 code) is absent or correctly refused. The rejection is not about carry. It is about the one thing this artifact does that its predecessors would not do — assign the DR-105 grant journal — and about what it left out while claiming completeness. The grant-journal assignment collides head-on with an owner-recorded disposition that says the Operational metadata class is 'not a grant journal', and the subject neither cites nor disposes of it. Separately, a durable byte named in the subject's own primary source, whose class assignment another live candidate expressly routes to DR-124, is not placed at all — which falsifies the subject's stated purpose. I want the coordinator to read B-1 precisely: I am not asking for the grant journal to be sent back to UNASSIGNED. Leaving it unassigned was the defect this artifact exists to cure, and curing it is right. The defect is that it was cured silently against a recorded contrary bound.

Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer and NOT A GRANT JOURNAL. Not rebuildable. ...'

The live file 08 DR-005 row (line 38) cites that identical digest as the 'effective disposition', 'plus operative rider RB-DR005-V2-A1 (if Operational metadata is denied, doctor fails closed; D-032 BLK-6; NO GRANT OR CLASS ADMISSION)'.
measurement.theOwnerRecording: D-060 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 2530), 'ADOPTED 2026-08-14', decision type RULE-GOVERNED, owner role 'Evidence, storage, and operability authorities', CONSENT from both independent reviewers at 0 MUST-FIX / 0 SHOULD-FIX. It records that exact digest plus that exact rider.
measurement.theSubjectDoesNotKnow: The subject's /recordedInputs/governingSources names only file 04 and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. The strings 'DR-005', 'D-060', 'P-005', 'RB-DR005' and 'preview-disposition' occur ZERO times in the subject. This is not a considered override; it is an unnoticed collision.
measurement.scopeCheck: P-005-2's surface line names the DR-124 class itself, with doctor's audit record as an INCLUDED member rather than the whole surface, so the 'not a grant journal' bound is class-scoped and not confined to doctor's own bytes. The rider's 'no grant or class admission' reinforces the same reading.

blockers.whyBlocker: DR-124's own row names its owners as 'Semantic/evidence/storage/lifecycle owners'. DR-005's disposition was recorded by the evidence, storage and operability authorities — an overlapping owner set — and it says in terms that this class is not a grant journal. A DR-124 candidate may well be the right instrument to supersede that bound; it is emphatically not entitled to contradict it silently. As the bytes stand, a coordinator who adopts this artifact adopts a class admission that a live, owner-recorded, independently consented disposition forbids, without either document acknowledging the other.
blockers.notARequestToLeaveItUnassigned: I am not asking for a reversion to UNASSIGNED. The dispatch lists 'leaving the grant journal unassigned' as an attack surface and I agree with that framing: the unassigned state is what strands doctor's FC-RO and DR-112's monotonic store. The repair is to make the assignment lawfully, not to withdraw it.
blockers.minimumRepair: Record route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v2.json (3b50bcf1…), D-060, and rider RB-DR005-V2-A1 as governing inputs. Then take one of two routes explicitly: (a) place the journal in a class P-005-2 does not bar, or (b) state that DR-124's closure supersedes P-005-2's 'not a grant journal' bound and the rider's 'no class admission', name the evidence/storage/operability authorities as the owners whose concurrence that supersession requires, and record it as a supersession with its reversibility cost — not as a fresh assignment on a blank field.

It is therefore neither discardable-and-rebuildable (SC-CACHE, whose rule is 'may be discarded/rebuilt') nor obviously excluded from Plan/Run (SC-OPS's rule).

blockers.whyBlocker: The purpose sentence is a completeness claim and it is false as measured. The consequence is not cosmetic: DR-112's live candidate is riding DR-124 for precisely this assignment, so a DR-124 closure that omits it leaves DR-112 riding a row that has closed without answering it — the same stranding pattern the grant journal suffered under D-032, reproduced on a second byte. There is also an unresolved fork the subject cannot leave silent: if this state is not operational metadata then it is analysis-affecting durable state, and D-002 records that slice 1 'takes on no analysis-affecting durable state class'. The subject's SC-ANALYSIS standing of 'OUT of slice 1' cannot be evaluated until this byte is placed one way or the other.
blockers.minimumRepair: Add a bytePlacement entry for trust roots / revocation observations / expiry floors / anti-rollback counters. Either assign a class with warrant, or record it as EXPRESSLY RESERVED naming DR-107 and DR-112 and stating that DR-124 does not settle it here — a reservation discharges the purpose sentence, an omission does not. If the honest answer is that it is analysis-affecting, say so and state the consequence for D-002's slice-1 scope rather than leaving the contradiction implicit. Do the same for the installed generation inventory and index custody records, or narrow the purpose sentence to the bytes actually covered.

blockers.title: SC-OPS is given a sole writer that is not the grant journal's sole writer, and the subject never identifies the two

measurement.classRule: File 04's Operational metadata row, carried verbatim by the subject itself: column 2 is 'Owner / SOLE WRITER' and its value is 'Core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner'; column 4 is 'Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer'.
measurement.theJournalsWriter: permission-truth-tables.v6.json /linearization/theOrder/carrier: 'ONE durable, append-only grant journal per (project, grant generation), with EXACTLY ONE WRITER: THE HOST, HOLDING THE PROJECT/OPERATION LOCK. There is no second ordering authority anywhere in this design.' /linearization/theOrder/sequence: 'Every record carries a strictly increasing unsigned integer sequence number assigned by the single writer.'
measurement.theSubjectNeverReconciles: The subject asserts the placement in one clause and never states that the DR-105 host permission broker IS the core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner, nor carves the journal out of the class's bounded/redacted rule.

blockers.whyBlocker: Two contracts each declare a SOLE writer for the same bytes and name different parties. If they are the same owner, that identification is exactly the kind of closure the DR-124 row demands ('Closed state-class/owner/writer architecture') and it must be stated, because DR-105's linearization rests on there being no second ordering authority. If they are not the same owner, the placement installs a second writer into a declared sole-writer class — which is NT-1, the cross-class-write negative test the subject itself lists at /negativeTests[0]. A contract whose whole subject is owner and writer closure cannot leave the writer identity of the one byte it newly places to inference. Secondarily and on the same clause: the class rule says these bytes are 'bounded' and 'redacted', while the journal must be durable and append-only with no record lost, since the sequence is the ordering authority. Bounding or redacting a monotonic journal drops records the linearization depends on. The subject does not address this either.
blockers.minimumRepair: State the writer identity explicitly — either 'the DR-105 host broker holding the project/operation lock IS the core lifecycle owner for these bytes, and DR-105's single-writer property is preserved', or place the journal where its writer is already the declared sole writer. In the same entry, state whether the class's 'journaled/redacted/bounded' rule applies to these bytes, and if it does not, record the carve-out as part of the assignment.

Placing the journal inside the Operational metadata root satisfies the first conjunct and fails the second, because grant-journal records are written by the host broker, not by doctor about its own invocation. Doctor v4 also states 'FC-RO's Operational metadata class root is only as well-defined as DR-124's closure makes it; if DR-124 closes by scoped disposition, the leg and the fixture's boundary follow that disposition's terms.'

This artifact is that closure and it moves FC-RO's failure from the first conjunct to the second without noticing. A harness author reading the assignment alone would reasonably conclude the collision is discharged; it is not.

coordinatorNote: Three blockers, and they are not three independent complaints — B-1 and B-3 are the same clause read two ways, and B-2 is the byte that clause forgot. The whole rejection lives in /bytePlacement. Everything else in this artifact is in good shape: the carry discipline is the best I have measured in this corpus, and I could not break the row-verbatim, the file 04 carry, the manifest fields, the negative-test set, the harness name, or any scoping disclaimer. Two things the coordinator should weigh. First, B-1 is a genuine authority question, not a drafting slip: DR-005's disposition and DR-124's candidate both speak to the same class, they disagree, and the DR-005 side is owner-recorded while this side is not. Whichever way it resolves, the two documents have to acknowledge each other before either can be relied on. Second, the fix for B-2 may be as small as one RESERVED entry — but it should not be waved through as hygiene, because the fork underneath it (operational metadata versus analysis-affecting) touches D-002's slice-1 scope, and that is a larger question than a missing line. I did not read the other reviewer's file, did not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, and did not commit.
